guides.title: Frontend Engineering
guides.description: From HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to application state, rendering architecture, accessibility, security, and production diagnosis.

parts.title: The browser: from a URL to an interactive page
parts.description: Follow navigation, resource discovery, rendering, and main-thread work to locate the dependency delaying a useful page.

parts.title: HTML, forms, and document contracts
parts.description: Use semantic structure, native forms, validation, and progressive enhancement as reliable contracts between users, browsers, and servers.

parts.title: CSS: cascade, layout, and resilient presentation
parts.description: Understand cascade ownership, intrinsic sizing, responsive layouts, stacking contexts, and the real costs of animation.

parts.title: JavaScript: execution, asynchronous work, and memory
parts.description: Reason about tasks, microtasks, object identity, workers, cancellation, reachability, and memory diagnosis.

parts.title: TypeScript, modules, and the build graph
parts.description: Model valid states, validate runtime boundaries, understand module graphs, and ship reproducible compatible assets.

parts.title: Components, state ownership, and React scheduling
parts.description: Place facts under clear owners, model transitions, preserve component identity, and distinguish rendering priority from parallel computation.

parts.title: Requests, caches, and consistency in the interface
parts.description: Handle stale responses, scoped caches, optimistic updates, concurrency conflicts, ambiguous writes, and changing paginated data.

parts.title: Navigation, SPAs, and application boundaries
parts.description: Explain why client navigation arose and preserve URLs, history, focus, route errors, and ownership as applications grow.

parts.title: CSR, SSR, SSG, and incremental regeneration
parts.description: Choose rendering time and location around freshness, personalization, hydration, cache scope, and deployment capabilities.

parts.title: Streaming, Server Components, and useful boundaries
parts.description: Design streaming and server/client boundaries around independent work, error isolation, serialization, and browser code budgets.

parts.title: Accessibility and design systems as engineering contracts
parts.description: Build reusable semantics, keyboard behavior, overlays, announcements, localization, and compatibility into shared components.

parts.title: Browser security and trust boundaries
parts.description: Separate origins, CORS, XSS, CSP, sessions, CSRF, private caching, and third-party authority into explicit security decisions.

parts.title: Performance, auditing, and production diagnosis
parts.description: Connect user experience to load and interaction traces, work through a concrete regression, and verify production outcomes by cohort.

parts.title: Realtime, browser storage, and offline behavior
parts.description: Choose transports, replay with versions, bound local storage, and define safe offline writes and service-worker upgrades.

parts.title: Testing, release safety, and architectural evolution
parts.description: Test meaningful invariants, control asynchronous failures, preserve old clients, and evolve frontend architecture through observable seams.

guides.title: Backend Engineering
guides.description: From request execution and trusted contracts to data correctness, distributed processing, and production recovery. Follow the mechanisms, failure schedules, and implementation tradeoffs behind reliable backends.

parts.title: Requests, protocols, and the server boundary
parts.description: Trace HTTP and gRPC from the connection to the handler, including proxy trust, deadlines, and protocol guarantees.

parts.title: Concurrency, scheduling, and backpressure
parts.description: Connect event loops, workers, cancellation, queues, and global pool budgets to useful work under overload.

parts.title: API contracts, representation, and pagination
parts.description: Design commands, errors, compatible representations, and stable list traversal with explicit consistency semantics.

parts.title: Identity, authorization, and tenant isolation
parts.description: Carry verified identity and resource permissions through queries, caches, jobs, and shared infrastructure.

parts.title: Domain rules, data models, and ownership
parts.description: Model invariants, historical facts, constraints, state transitions, and the owner of each durable decision.

parts.title: Storage engines, indexes, and query plans
parts.description: Read storage and query costs through WAL, MVCC maintenance, access paths, plans, and representative cardinalities.

parts.title: Transactions, MVCC, and concurrency control
parts.description: Work through last-unit races, snapshot isolation, write skew, locks, version checks, and ambiguous commits.

parts.title: Caches, freshness, and invalidation
parts.description: Make cache identity, stale-fill races, stampedes, eviction, and cache-outage capacity part of one contract.

parts.title: Deadlines, retries, and idempotent operations
parts.description: Bound failure amplification and resolve uncertain mutations using budgets, receipts, stable operation IDs, and reconciliation.

parts.title: Queues, streams, and transactional messaging
parts.description: Understand durable acceptance, outbox and inbox transactions, ordering, redelivery, replay, and backlog drain.

parts.title: Replication, partitioning, and identifiers
parts.description: Reason about replica lag, failover, shard ownership, routing epochs, global operations, and identifier guarantees.

parts.title: Coordination, leases, and durable workflows
parts.description: See why expired owners need fencing and how persistent workflow state handles cross-system uncertainty and compensation.

parts.title: Search indexes and derived data
parts.description: Build a search read model with permission-aware retrieval, versioned updates, deletion rules, rebuild boundaries, and reconciliation.

parts.title: Realtime delivery, batch jobs, and resumable work
parts.description: Choose polling, SSE, or WebSockets and make reconnects, snapshot gaps, slow consumers, and export checkpoints explicit.

parts.title: Service boundaries and safe evolution
parts.description: Use ownership to choose modules or services, then evolve schema, events, caches, and deployments without breaking overlap.

parts.title: Testing, observability, and capacity reasoning
parts.description: Connect invariants to race tests, useful telemetry, critical-path diagnosis, realistic load, and operating budgets.

parts.title: Worked production reviews
parts.description: Review a recoverable checkout and an isolated large-tenant export using concrete budgets, crash schedules, and recovery evidence.

guides.title: AI Engineering
guides.description: From learning, tokens, and attention to retrieval, adaptation, GPU serving, evaluated agents, and production systems.

parts.title: Language models, tokens, and generation
parts.description: Choose the right computation, then follow tokenization, representations, next-token probabilities, decoding, and context limits.

parts.title: How models learn
parts.description: Features, objectives, gradients, generalization, next-token training, optimization memory, distributed training, and post-training incentives.

parts.title: Inside a transformer
parts.description: Trace tensor shapes through Q/K/V attention, masks, positions, residuals, feed-forward blocks, MoE, and cached generation.

parts.title: Instructions, structured output, and reasoning
parts.description: Version task contracts, organize context, constrain output shape, verify reasoning artifacts, and bound refinement loops.

parts.title: Data, fine-tuning, and adaptation
parts.description: Diagnose when training helps, curate reproducible data, understand SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, distillation, and adaptation releases.

parts.title: Embeddings and vector indexes
parts.description: Understand representation contracts, similarity geometry, exact baselines, HNSW/IVF, filtering, migrations, and retrieval quality.

parts.title: Retrieval and evidence-grounded generation
parts.description: Build versioned ingestion, meaningful chunks, hybrid search, reranking, context packing, advanced RAG, and permission-safe evidence reuse.

parts.title: Evaluation that supports engineering decisions
parts.description: Define task outcomes, fixtures, component metrics, calibrated judges, statistical uncertainty, paired comparisons, and release gates.

parts.title: GPU inference, memory, and scheduling
parts.description: Work through serving phases, weight/KV memory, FlashAttention, paging, batching, quantization, speculation, and parallelism.

parts.title: Model selection and serving economics
parts.description: Compare complete systems, calculate cost per accepted outcome, assess routing/cascades, and choose hosted or self-hosted capacity.

parts.title: Agents, tools, and durable execution
parts.description: Bound agent control, design domain tools, integrate MCP, make effects idempotent, recover durable tasks, and manage memory and coordination.

parts.title: AI security and data boundaries
parts.description: Trace prompt injection and data exposure across retrieval, tools, caches, memory, execution environments, and derived artifacts.

parts.title: Images, audio, and realtime interaction
parts.description: Handle visual representations, OCR/layout, video sampling, voice pipelines, turn cancellation, audio transport, and image generation.

parts.title: Production architecture, releases, and worked designs
parts.description: Set outcome SLOs, trace failures, release compatible system versions, and work through a private knowledge assistant and an operations agent.

guides.title: DevOps
guides.description: From supervised processes and traffic routing to repeatable artifacts, infrastructure, Kubernetes, and reliable production operations.

parts.title: Processes and the first deployment
parts.description: Process identity, supervision, shutdown, resource budgets, and the limits of a single host.

parts.title: DNS, TLS, and the traffic path
parts.description: Follow DNS, TCP, TLS, proxies, load balancers, and private routes to isolate a failing request.

parts.title: Git, CI, and artifact promotion
parts.description: Change graphs, CI trust boundaries, build provenance, and promotion of one verified artifact.

parts.title: Containers and image builds
parts.description: Understand image layers, isolation, resource limits, build inputs, secrets, and process lifecycle.

parts.title: Cloud identity, networks, and managed services
parts.description: Choose compute and storage models, scope cloud identities, and design network and failure boundaries.

parts.title: Terraform, state, and infrastructure changes
parts.description: Configuration, state bindings, plans, locks, drift, imports, refactors, and partial apply recovery.

parts.title: Kubernetes reconciliation and workloads
parts.description: Trace reconciliation, scheduling, workloads, resource budgets, storage, and workload identities.

parts.title: Services, probes, and graceful traffic changes
parts.description: Connect Service routing, readiness, liveness, endpoint propagation, and graceful replacement.

parts.title: Helm, GitOps, and safe releases
parts.description: Chart contracts, reconciliation ownership, progressive delivery, and compatible schema evolution.

parts.title: Capacity, autoscaling, and overload
parts.description: Model throughput and headroom, understand HPA feedback, and protect constrained dependencies.

parts.title: Platform security and the software supply chain
parts.description: Trace build trust, provenance, runtime privileges, workload credentials, and compromise recovery.

parts.title: Observability, SLOs, and incident response
parts.description: Define useful SLIs, reason about telemetry, diagnose boundaries, and coordinate recovery.

parts.title: Backups, disaster recovery, and stateful operations
parts.description: Plan RPO/RTO, application-consistent restores, failover authority, and recovery verification.

guides.title: Last Mile Prep
guides.description: Handle incidents, turn ambiguous requests into product decisions, and measure what reaches production.

parts.title: Incident triage: scope, stabilize, and communicate
parts.description: Establish impact, coordinate responders, choose a safe mitigation, and verify the customer journey.

parts.title: Production debugging: test a hypothesis at each boundary
parts.description: Use traces, resource evidence, database activity, and browser context to distinguish competing explanations.

parts.title: Reliability, recovery, and incident learning
parts.description: Set useful SLOs, verify reconciliation and backlog recovery, and turn incidents into owned improvements.

parts.title: Requirements, audience, and engineering judgment
parts.description: Understand the customer job and audience, make system promises explicit, and choose a complete first slice.

parts.title: A/B tests and product evidence
parts.description: Separate rollout safety from causal inference, define credible outcomes, and interpret experimental uncertainty.

parts.title: Feature flags and controlled releases
parts.description: Separate deployment from exposure, preserve assignment across work, and manage fallback, rollout, and flag removal.

parts.title: Deprecating features without abandoning users
parts.description: Find dependents, define migration and compatibility, communicate sunset, and prove the removal gate.

parts.title: Signals, structured logs, and trace context
parts.description: Design logs, metrics, traces, and asynchronous context with bounded cardinality and useful evidence.

parts.title: Operational telemetry: Grafana, New Relic, Sentry, and replay
parts.description: Navigate operational evidence with Grafana, New Relic, Sentry, Honeybadger, and FullStory.

parts.title: Product analytics: PostHog, Pendo, and GA4
parts.description: Define outcome events, identity, funnels, and collection contracts that support trustworthy product decisions.
